note: Story: problem -> how HeatOps fixes it -> how it runs on AWS. {tokens} are filled from asset-manifest facts. Scene audio starts at scene start + leadSeconds. Run `npm run voice` after editing. A '||' marker inserts a beat (1 s, or pauseSeconds per scene).

scenes.S01: Tomorrow, {workers} workers are scheduled outdoors at Yamuna Works in Delhi. By one p.m., it will feel like forty-one degrees, right when half the day's work is planned. A heat warning tells you it's going to be hot. It doesn't tell you what to change, who needs to know, or whether anyone actually did it.
scenes.S02: This is HeatOps. The night before, the supervisor sees tomorrow's plan against the forecast: every crew, every task, and every hour that lands in the heat.
scenes.S03: One click, and the HeatOps agent gets to work. || It pulls the forecast, reads the site's constraints, and compares schedules that actually fit. Its first idea: start Crew A at six, before the heat builds.
scenes.S04: But the supervisor knows something the forecast doesn't. The gate doesn't open until seven. || So they change it. || The old plan is instantly marked outdated, and the agent replans around the new constraint. || Crew A now starts at seven. And the hours still in the heat aren't hidden. They're flagged for a decision.
scenes.S05: The result: work in the heat window drops from {baseline} worker-hours to {revised}, and all {taskHours} hours of work still get done. The remaining {revised} stay on the supervisor's radar.
scenes.S06: One approval turns the plan into action. HeatOps assigns a schedule notice, readiness checks for water and shade, and a follow-up for the remaining risk. On site, the supervisor confirms they've read it, and reports when the crew is actually ready.
scenes.S07: And if a check is missed? || HeatOps doesn't assume. The task goes overdue, and lands on the operations lead's board.
scenes.S08: Under the hood, it's all AWS. The web app on Amplify talks to API Gateway and Lambda. Planning runs as a background job through SQS, where a Strands agent calls Amazon Bedrock and our scheduling tools. Every plan, revision, and audit event lives in DynamoDB. And every minute, EventBridge checks for anything that's slipped.
scenes.S09: And here's that same run in CloudWatch. One run ID, end to end.
scenes.S10: HeatOps. Tomorrow's heat forecast. Tonight's action plan.
